turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, sorry, the auto got stuck near the market, so we are late. My father stays with me. He has gone down twice this week and I am really worried.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Arre, don't start all that. I did not fall. I slid down, that is all. I am alright.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, uncle. I want it in your words. When was the first one?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Tuesday, I think. I was getting up from the plastic chair, the mat slipped, and I sat on the floor. No cut, no bleeding.
[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The second was Thursday, near ten at night, by the bathroom. I heard the sound. He was holding the wall.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The floor was a little wet, na. So I slid. If I am sitting down myself, how is that a fall?
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Before you went down, did you black out, even for a moment?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I never lost consciousness. And there is no giddiness also. I am perfectly fine, these things happen in a house.
[SEG0009] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, that is not fair. Yesterday morning you told me the room was going round when you got out of bed.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Achha, that. Only if I get up fast. One or two seconds the head spins, then it settles itself. Mostly in the morning, and it is nothing, doctor.

[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Especially in the morning, if you stand up quickly, you spin for a couple of seconds and it passes. And twice this week you ended on the floor, which you are calling a slide, not a fall.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, put it like that. Two seconds, three seconds, not more. Since when it started I cannot say. Maybe only this week, maybe from before, I never marked the date.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with this giddiness?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no chest pain. Chest is okay.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): And breathlessness?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I walk up to the gate. Breathing is normal.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does the vision go dark, or does the heart race?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Heart is not racing. Yesterday morning, when I stood up, it became a little dim in front of the eyes, then it came back. I held the cot, and I did not go down.
[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also the left knee, doctor. On Thursday he knocked it on the door and he keeps rubbing it, but he will say it is zero.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Knee is not needing all this. Little ache when I bend, that is all. I don't want any operation talk.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fine, a little ache in the left knee on bending. Any weakness on one side, arm or leg or the face, even for a minute?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing like that. Both hands are working. I made my own tea.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Urine, motions, any change? Any fever?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): All normal only. No fever. Appetite is also good. My daughter feeds me too much, that is the real problem.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tell me the tablets. Blood pressure ones first, then anything for sleep.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Morning, amlodipine five mg. Night, telmisartan forty mg. And hydrochlorothiazide twelve point five in the morning, the water tablet, after the amlodipine. All for the BP, for years.
[SEG0027] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I fill his box, that part is correct. And clonazepam zero point five at night, for sleep. He has been on it a long time.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Not every night, please. Only when sleep is not coming. Some weeks four nights, some weeks three. I am not sitting and eating it daily.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any diabetes tablets, or painkillers?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, thankfully. Ecosprin seventy five, one after lunch, for many years. They did angioplasty and put one stent in two thousand sixteen. After that, Ecosprin is continuing.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine? Rash, swelling, breathing trouble?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I can take whatever you give.
[SEG0033] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, sulfa. Around twenty eighteen you got a rash with a sulfa antibiotic and they stopped it. You yourself said never take sulfa again.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): That was so long back, I don't even remember it properly. Maybe the tablet, maybe just the summer heat. I am not sure it was an allergy at all.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. I will treat sulfa as a possible reaction that is not fully clear, and I will not prescribe any sulfa. Sister, did you manage the lying and standing pressures?

[SEG0036] person_4 (NURSE): Yes, doctor. Lying, the blood pressure was one thirty eight over eighty two with a pulse of seventy four, and after one minute of standing it was one hundred and four over sixty eight with a pulse of eighty eight. He caught my arm and said his head was spinning just then. Saturation was ninety eight percent on room air, and the temperature was thirty six point six.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Uncle, from one thirty eight down to one oh four on standing, that is a real drop. Face is symmetrical, and the grip is equal in both hands. Heart sounds are normal with no murmur, and the lungs are clear.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): See, I am fine only. There is a serial at seven, can we finish?
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, two minutes. Let him speak.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud so both of you hear where I will not jump. This can be the pressure falling when you stand, from the three blood pressure tablets, or the clonazepam making balance worse at night. I am not concluding a stroke, and I am not ready to call it an inner-ear problem. My working impression is postural hypotension, though I cannot rule out the sleeping tablet adding to the Thursday night episode.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): You will stop all the BP tablets then? The pressure will go high, no?

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not all of them. I am changing only the amlodipine, from tomorrow two point five milligram every morning instead of five. Telmisartan forty at night, hydrochlorothiazide twelve point five in the morning, and Ecosprin seventy five after lunch, all those stay. Clonazepam remains zero point five, only on the nights you truly cannot sleep, and do not take more.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Half of the five mg tablet, morning. That much I understood.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Sit at the edge of the cot for a full minute before you stand. Keep drinking water in the day, unless your feet swell. No scooter for now, even to the temple.
[SEG0045] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will keep the scooter key with me, doctor. He still sneaks out some mornings.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Today, before you leave, blood tests for sodium, potassium and creatinine, plus an ECG, and if you slide down again or black out we might scan the head, but not today. Come back to my OPD in two weeks with the reports. If the giddiness gets worse before that, or you go down again, come earlier, do not wait two weeks.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
